category: Usenet search engine (undocumented JSON search API, anonymous NZB download)

free_tier.stated: No account and no key. GET /api/search?q=linux returned 7,318 bytes of JSON: 25 items, totalElements 4,348 over 174 pages. GET /download/<item-id>.nzb returned a 4,264-byte NZB. The route is what the site's own single-page app calls; no API documentation was found on any page reached.
free_tier.notes: No quota is published, and no account exists to attach one to. 6 rapid requests and 1 download in one session produced no 429.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the answer is an NZB pointer file (4,264 bytes), never the payload

retention.stated: not stated on the pages read. A third-party indexer comparison claims 'approximately 1,900 days retention, 900+ newsgroups indexed' (nzbhydra.com, 2026-10-23).

egress.terms: No metering. The JSON is a result list and the download is an XML pointer file measured at 4,264 bytes.

interface_detail: The search page is a client-rendered Next.js app: /search?q=linux returns 8,702 bytes of HTML shell with zero results and an empty query state. The real interface is GET /api/search?q=<query>, which returns JSON with data.content[] and data.page{size,number,totalElements,totalPages}. NZB download is GET /download/<item-id>.nzb.
tooling: No Newznab endpoint, so Prowlarr, NZBHydra2, Sonarr and Radarr cannot add it directly. A wrapper is small: one GET for JSON, one GET per download, both unauthenticated. The JSON route is undocumented and can change with any front-end deploy, which is the maintenance cost.
chaining: A second unnamed fallback beside Binsearch, and the only one of the three open engines with a JSON answer, so it is the easiest to wrap and the one to poll when a name has to be resolved without an account.

limits.value: none observed: 6 consecutive JSON searches in one session, all 200

limits_note: Page size is fixed at 25 in the JSON the app consumes (data.page.size = 25); there is no limit parameter to raise it.
binding_note: No byte counter, no daily cap, no account. At 1 TiB/month the indexer is not the constraint; the news provider's retention is, and a missing post costs a failed grab rather than a quota.

identity_cost.detail: Nothing is collected: both the JSON search and the NZB download answered without a cookie, header or key.

reliability_note: Advertiser-supported; the JSON route is an internal app call, so a front-end deploy can move or rename it without notice, and a scrape that depended on it fails silently as an empty result list.
confidence_note: Search and download were run today with status, byte count and digest recorded. The undocumented route is the fragility, not the confidence rung: it worked when measured and may not tomorrow.

evidence.proved: anonymous JSON search returned 200 and 7,318 bytes: 25 items, totalElements 4,348, 174 pages
anonymous NZB download returned 200, application/x-nzb, 4,264 bytes (sha256 12eb9715...)
the HTML page carries no results: 8,702 bytes of app shell with "q":"" in the serialised state, which is why a scraper must use /api/search

notes: Adding ?x=1 made the path valid and the download worked.
